alphabet.title: One letter, a different word
alphabet.goal: Compare n with ñ as distinct letters.

frames.label: Read the n
frames.explanation: Campana contains n. The highlighted letter belongs to the word, not a separate syllable.

frames.label: Change n to ñ
frames.explanation: Campaña contains ñ. The tilde changes the letter and consonant sound; it is not a stress accent.

alphabet.title: Read ll as one consonant spelling
alphabet.goal: Keep the spelling together while recognizing it in two story words.

frames.label: Find the spelling
frames.explanation: Ll in llave is one consonant spelling, not two English l sounds. Follow the audio’s regional model.

frames.label: Recognize it inside a word
frames.explanation: The same ll spelling appears inside calle. Regional ll/y pronunciation varies; this diagram shows spelling, not sound.

vowels.title: Keep both vowels clear
vowels.goal: Separate vowel identity from syllable stress.

frames.label: Read the word
frames.explanation: The highlighted u and a each keep a recognizable vowel sound.

frames.label: Notice the unstressed vowel
frames.explanation: The final a is unstressed, but it remains a clear a. This spelling diagram does not produce the sound.

stress.title: Find the prominent syllable
stress.goal: Compare the default stress patterns with an accent override.

frames.label: Default stress
frames.explanation: Hablo ends in a vowel with no written accent: HA-blo.

frames.label: Accent moves the stress
frames.explanation: The accent puts stress on the final syllable: ha-BLÓ. This is also a different verb form.

rr.title: One r or two?
rr.goal: See where the sound contrast occurs between vowels.

frames.label: A quick tap
frames.explanation: Between vowels, a single r normally represents the tap.

frames.label: A trill
frames.explanation: Between vowels, rr represents the trill. The added letter changes the word; this diagram is not a pronunciation recording.

gender.title: Let the noun guide the endings
gender.goal: Follow feminine agreement from the noun to the article and adjective.

frames.label: Masculine noun
frames.explanation: Libro is masculine; el and nuevo agree with it.

frames.label: Change the noun
frames.explanation: Mesa is feminine, so the article and adjective change. The noun chooses the agreement.

articles.title: Introduce it, then identify it
articles.goal: Watch an indefinite article become definite after the book is introduced.

frames.label: Introduce a book
frames.explanation: Un introduces one book that has not yet been identified.

frames.label: Refer back to it
frames.explanation: The listener now knows which book: the one just introduced.

plural.title: Number travels across the phrase
plural.goal: Change singular to plural and follow all three agreement changes.

frames.label: One book
frames.explanation: The article, noun and adjective are singular.

frames.label: More than one
frames.explanation: All three words change. Do not pluralize only the noun.

adjectives.title: Match the description
adjectives.goal: Compare an adjective that changes gender with one that does not.

frames.label: Masculine singular
frames.explanation: Interesante has the same form for masculine and feminine singular nouns.

frames.label: Feminine singular
frames.explanation: The adjective stays interesante even though the noun is feminine.

frames.label: Feminine plural
frames.explanation: Gender did not change this adjective, but plural number adds -s.

comparisons.title: Quality or quantity?
comparisons.goal: Choose the comparison pattern based on the kind of information.

frames.label: Start here
frames.spanish: Ana es más alta que Luis.
frames.explanation: Más…que compares unequal height.

frames.label: See the change
frames.spanish: Ana es tan alta como Luis.
frames.english: Ana is as tall as Luis.
frames.explanation: Tan…como expresses equal height.

frames.label: Start here
frames.english: I have as many books as you.
frames.explanation: Tantos agrees with masculine plural libros.

frames.label: See the change
frames.english: I have as many questions as you.
frames.explanation: Tantas agrees with feminine plural preguntas.

subject-pronouns.title: The ending carries the subject
subject-pronouns.goal: Remove an optional pronoun while keeping a complete sentence.

frames.label: Make the subject explicit
frames.explanation: Yo explicitly names the subject; -o already identifies the speaker.

frames.label: Let the verb identify the speaker
frames.explanation: The pronoun disappears, but the sentence is complete. Keep yo when useful for contrast or clarity.

tu-usted.title: Change the relationship, change the form
tu-usted.goal: Keep the addressee and verb consistent.

frames.label: Informal singular you
frames.explanation: Tú uses the -as ending for hablar.

frames.label: Formal singular you
frames.explanation: Usted addresses you but takes the same verb form as él/ella.

possessives.title: Count the things, not the owners
possessives.goal: Keep the owner fixed while the possessed noun changes.

frames.label: One thing
frames.explanation: Mi refers to one possessed thing.

frames.label: Several things
frames.explanation: The owner remains the speaker. Mis changes because libros is plural.

object-pronouns.title: Replace it, then move it
object-pronouns.goal: Follow the object as a noun phrase becomes a pronoun before the verb.

frames.label: Find the object
frames.explanation: El libro receives the action. It is masculine singular.

frames.label: Choose its replacement
frames.explanation: Lo replaces el libro. This intermediate frame isolates a pronoun; it is not a complete sentence.

frames.label: Put it before the verb
frames.explanation: The object pronoun comes before the conjugated verb, unlike the full noun phrase.

reflexive.title: Keep the subject linked to itself
reflexive.goal: Change both the pronoun and verb when changing the subject.

frames.label: The speaker acts on themself
frames.explanation: Yo, me and lavo point to the same person.

frames.label: Address the listener
frames.explanation: Change yo → tú, me → te and lavo → lavas together.

infinitives.title: Only the first verb carries the person
infinitives.goal: Change the subject while leaving the wanted action in its dictionary form.

frames.label: I want to eat
frames.explanation: Quiero carries the subject; comer names the action.

frames.label: You want to eat
frames.explanation: Quiero becomes quieres. Comer stays in the infinitive.

present-ar.title: Build the verb, one piece at a time
present-ar.goal: Choose a subject and watch the dictionary ending become a personal ending.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies yo. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies tú. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies nosotros. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

present-er-ir.title: Build the verb, one piece at a time
present-er-ir.goal: Choose a subject and watch the dictionary ending become a personal ending.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies yo. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies tú. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies nosotros. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

frames.label: The -ir family
frames.explanation: Vivir belongs to the -ir family.

frames.label: The we form
frames.explanation: Compare comemos with vivimos: the nosotros ending differs by family.

ser-estar.title: One adjective, two messages
ser-estar.goal: Change the verb while holding the person and adjective still.

frames.label: Characterize the person
frames.explanation: Ser presents aburrido as a characteristic.

frames.label: Describe his state
frames.explanation: Estar presents a state. The English interpretation changes with the verb.

hay.title: Introduce something, then locate it
hay.goal: Distinguish existence from the location of an identified thing.

frames.label: Introduce a pharmacy
frames.explanation: Hay introduces a pharmacy’s existence. Una introduces the noun.

frames.label: Locate the known pharmacy
frames.explanation: La identifies the pharmacy; está locates it.

ir-future.title: Build a future plan
ir-future.goal: Change the person on ir while keeping a + infinitive.

frames.label: Start here
frames.explanation: Voy matches yo. A connects ir to the infinitive.

frames.label: See the change
frames.explanation: Only the personal form of ir changes: vas. A estudiar stays.

frames.label: Start here
frames.explanation: Vamos identifies we.

frames.label: See the change
frames.explanation: Van identifies they; the planned action stays comer.

preterite.title: Build a completed past form
preterite.goal: Choose a subject and watch the dictionary ending become a personal ending.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies yo. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies tú. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies ella. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

imperfect.title: Build a past habit
imperfect.goal: Choose a subject and watch the dictionary ending become a personal ending.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies yo. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

frames.label: Start with the infinitive
frames.explanation: The dictionary ending identifies the verb family.

frames.label: Keep the stem
frames.explanation: Remove the infinitive ending. This is a building piece, not a complete verb form.

frames.label: Attach the personal ending
frames.explanation: The new ending identifies nosotros. Read the stem and ending together as one word.

past-contrast.title: Background meets an event
past-contrast.goal: See ongoing background and a completed event in the same past scene.

frames.label: Set the scene
frames.explanation: The imperfect shows the rain from inside the situation, without asserting its start or endpoint.

frames.label: Add the event
frames.english: It was raining when I left.
frames.explanation: Salí presents leaving as a completed event within the rainy background. Track edges show only the scene window, not the true start/end of the rain.

future.title: The future keeps the infinitive
future.goal: Keep the whole infinitive and attach the new ending.

frames.label: Keep the whole infinitive
frames.explanation: Unlike present-tense conjugation, keep the infinitive ending.

frames.label: Attach the ending
frames.explanation: Attach é to the whole infinitive. The base remains hablar.

frames.label: Keep the whole infinitive
frames.explanation: Unlike present-tense conjugation, keep the infinitive ending.

frames.label: Attach the ending
frames.explanation: Attach ás to the whole infinitive. The base remains hablar.

frames.label: Keep the whole infinitive
frames.explanation: Unlike present-tense conjugation, keep the infinitive ending.

frames.label: Attach the ending
frames.explanation: Attach emos to the whole infinitive. The base remains hablar.

conditional.title: Attach an imagined-result ending
conditional.goal: Keep the whole infinitive and attach the new ending.

frames.label: Keep the whole infinitive
frames.explanation: Unlike present-tense conjugation, keep the infinitive ending.

frames.label: Attach the ending
frames.explanation: Attach ía to the whole infinitive. The base remains comer.

frames.label: Keep the whole infinitive
frames.explanation: Unlike present-tense conjugation, keep the infinitive ending.

frames.label: Attach the ending
frames.explanation: Attach íamos to the whole infinitive. The base remains comer.

subjunctive.title: Change the stance, change the mood
subjunctive.goal: Compare affirmative belief with a negated belief.

frames.label: Assert a belief
frames.explanation: Affirmative creo que normally presents the belief with indicative tiene.

frames.label: Withhold the belief
frames.english: I do not think she has time.
frames.explanation: No creo que normally takes subjunctive tenga here. Tener changes its stem too; this is not a rule that every negative sentence takes subjunctive.

word-order.title: Follow the sentence roles
word-order.goal: Remove a clear subject without removing the action or object.

frames.label: Name all three roles
frames.explanation: Yo is the subject, compro the verb and pan the direct object.

frames.label: Omit a clear subject
frames.explanation: Compro still identifies the speaker. The sentence does not need an explicit yo.

questions.title: Frame the question
questions.goal: Add question marks without adding an English-style helper verb.

frames.label: A statement
frames.explanation: The words state something.

frames.label: A direct question
frames.explanation: Opening and closing marks frame the same words. In speech, question intonation supplies the cue; the animation itself does not demonstrate the sound.

negatives.title: Put no before the pronoun group
negatives.goal: Negate a sentence without splitting the object pronoun from its verb.

frames.label: Affirmative
frames.explanation: Lo comes before the conjugated verb.

frames.label: Negative
frames.explanation: Add no before lo veo. No English-style do not helper is needed.

connecting.title: Reason and result point in different directions
connecting.goal: Reorder two ideas and choose the connector that preserves the relationship.

frames.label: Introduce the reason
frames.english: I study because I have an exam.
frames.explanation: Porque introduces the reason: having an exam.

frames.label: Introduce the result
frames.spanish: Tengo un examen; por eso estudio.
frames.english: I have an exam; that is why I study.
frames.explanation: Por eso introduces the consequence: studying. The logical relationship stays, but the order and connector change.

por-para.title: Recipient or reason?
por-para.goal: Keep the surrounding words and inspect the relationship expressed by the preposition.

frames.label: Intended recipient
frames.explanation: Para highlights you as the intended recipient or beneficiary.

frames.label: Motivating reason
frames.english: I do it for your sake.
frames.explanation: Por highlights you as the motivating reason. This contrast does not cover every use of either preposition.

gustar.title: The liked thing controls the verb
gustar.goal: Pluralize the thing liked while keeping the experiencer unchanged.

frames.label: One liked thing
frames.explanation: Me names the experiencer; singular libro controls gusta.

frames.label: Several liked things
frames.explanation: Me stays the same. Plural libros changes gusta to gustan.

commands.title: Attach it—or move it before
commands.goal: Compare pronoun placement and verb form in affirmative and negative tú commands.

frames.label: Affirmative command
frames.explanation: Lo attaches to the affirmative command. The written accent preserves stress.

frames.label: Negative command
frames.explanation: Lo moves before the verb. The negative tú command uses leas, not lee.

accent-marks.title: Move the stress, change the form
accent-marks.goal: See the written accent and stressed syllable change together.

frames.label: Default stress
frames.explanation: Hablo ends in a vowel with no written accent: HA-blo.

frames.label: Accent moves the stress
frames.explanation: The accent puts stress on the final syllable: ha-BLÓ. This is also a different verb form.

punctuation.title: Where does the question begin?
punctuation.goal: Keep the name outside the question and frame only the question itself.

frames.label: First, the statement
frames.explanation: Ana is direct address. The remainder is currently a statement.

frames.label: Ask the question
frames.explanation: The opening mark goes after the name, where the question begins.

se.title: Track what se is doing
se.goal: Compare agreement and pronoun replacement in distinct se constructions.

frames.label: Start here
frames.explanation: Passive-like se: singular casa agrees with vende.

frames.label: See the change
frames.explanation: Plural casas agrees with venden. Se itself does not change.

frames.label: Start here
frames.english: I give him/her/you formal the book.
frames.explanation: Le marks the recipient; el libro is the object.

frames.label: See the change
frames.english: I give it to him/her/you formal.
frames.explanation: El libro becomes lo before doy; le becomes se before lo. This is not reflexive se.

hypotheticals.title: Pair the condition with its result
hypotheticals.goal: Choose an open possibility or an imagined situation and compare both verb clauses.

frames.label: Start here
frames.english: If I have time, I will go.
frames.explanation: Open possibility: present indicative in the si clause; future in this result.

frames.label: See the change
frames.english: If I had time, I would go.
frames.explanation: Imagined situation: imperfect subjunctive in the condition and conditional in the result.

frames.label: Start here
frames.spanish: Si hubiera tenido tiempo, habría ido.
frames.english: If I had had time, I would have gone.
frames.explanation: Unreal completed past: hubiera + participle pairs with habría + participle.

frames.label: See the change
frames.english: If I had studied, I would have passed.
frames.explanation: Change the actions while keeping the same compound-tense pattern.

letter-combinations.title: Read ll as one consonant spelling
letter-combinations.goal: Keep the spelling together while recognizing it in two story words.

frames.label: Find the spelling
frames.explanation: Ll in llave is one consonant spelling, not two English l sounds. Follow the audio’s regional model.

frames.label: Recognize it inside a word
frames.explanation: The same ll spelling appears inside calle. Regional ll/y pronunciation varies; this diagram shows spelling, not sound.

syllables.title: Count the beats, then find the stress
syllables.goal: Syllables group sounds; one beat is prominent.

frames.label: Two syllables
frames.explanation: Ca-sa has two beats; ca is prominent.

frames.label: Four syllables
frames.explanation: Te-lé-fo-no has four beats; the accent marks lé.

vowel-combinations.title: One syllable together—or two apart
vowel-combinations.goal: A stressed closed vowel can separate from its neighbor.

frames.label: Shared vowel syllable
frames.explanation: Ha-cia has two syllables; ia shares a syllable.

frames.label: Stressed í separates
frames.explanation: Ha-cí-a has three syllables. The accent and meaning distinguish hacía from hacia.

sentence-emphasis.title: Same spelling, a different focus
sentence-emphasis.goal: Move sentence focus while preserving every word’s normal stress.

frames.label: Contrast who
frames.explanation: Highlighting yo can contrast who has it; no new written accent is needed.

frames.label: Contrast what
frames.english: I have the key. (Not the map.)
frames.explanation: The object is now the contrast. The words and their lexical stress do not change; listen to audio for actual intonation.

location-prepositions.title: Position or destination?
location-prepositions.goal: Read basic location and movement phrases, including multiword prepositions.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: En locates the speaker.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.english: I am going to the hotel.
frames.explanation: A marks the destination and contracts with el.

time-prepositions.title: Tell the time or schedule an event
time-prepositions.goal: Use common time phrases and connect an action to before or after another.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: This states the time.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.spanish: El tren sale a las ocho.
frames.explanation: A las attaches the clock time to an action.

indirect-objects.title: Count the recipients
indirect-objects.goal: Identify recipients and choose me, te, le, nos or les.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.spanish: Le doy un libro a Ana.
frames.explanation: One recipient takes le.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.spanish: Les doy un libro a Ana y Luis.
frames.english: I give Ana and Luis a book.
frames.explanation: Two recipients take les, even with one book.

pronoun-combinations.title: Choose both roles, then combine
pronoun-combinations.goal: Le changes to se before lo.

frames.label: Identify the recipient
frames.explanation: Le marks the recipient; el libro is the direct object.

frames.label: Replace the thing and adjust le
frames.explanation: Lo replaces the book before the verb. Le becomes se before lo; this is not reflexive se.

irregular-present.title: An ending change can include a stem change
irregular-present.goal: Compare the common stem pattern with nosotros.

frames.label: I can
frames.explanation: Poder changes o to ue in puedo.

frames.label: We can
frames.explanation: Nosotros keeps the original stem vowel o. Do not apply the change to every person.

irregular-preterite.title: Learn the new stem with its endings
irregular-preterite.goal: A strong preterite uses a shared stem and unaccented ending set.

frames.label: I had
frames.explanation: Tener uses tuv- and -e here.

frames.label: They had
frames.explanation: Keep tuv- and attach -ieron. The strong-stem endings differ from regular accented preterites.

demonstratives.title: A noun can be expressed or understood
demonstratives.goal: Match demonstratives to nouns and recover omitted nouns from context.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: The noun llave is explicit.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.explanation: Context supplies the omitted noun; esta remains feminine.

relative-clauses.title: Find the main action beneath the description
relative-clauses.goal: The relative clause attaches to the girl; it is not another main event.

frames.label: Read the core event
frames.explanation: Encontraron is the main verb; a una niña is the object.

frames.label: Attach her description
frames.spanish: Encontraron a una niña que sostenía una vela.
frames.english: They found a girl who was holding a candle.
frames.explanation: Que sostenía una vela describes niña. Find its verb without losing the main verb encontraron.

content-clauses.title: Content or description?
content-clauses.goal: Distinguish content clauses, indirect questions and relative descriptions.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.english: He/she says that he/she has a book.
frames.explanation: Que introduces the statement’s content.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.english: He/she reads the book that he/she has.
frames.explanation: Que introduces a description attached to libro.

participles.title: Completed action or resulting state?
participles.goal: Form common participles and decide whether agreement is required.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: Haber forms a tense; cerrado remains unchanged.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.explanation: Estar presents a state; cerradas agrees with puertas.

present-perfect.title: The auxiliary carries the person
present-perfect.goal: Keep the participle unchanged when changing who acts.

frames.label: One speaker
frames.explanation: He matches yo. Leído is a fixed participle.

frames.label: Several speakers
frames.explanation: Hemos changes the subject to we; leído does not change.

pluperfect.title: Same participle, different time relationship
pluperfect.goal: Recognize the earlier past and track its relationship to the story’s reference point.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: Present reference.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.english: Ana had gone out when I arrived.
frames.explanation: Leaving is earlier than another past event.

progressive.title: Change reference time, keep the activity
progressive.goal: Estar supplies time and person; the gerund stays the same.

frames.label: At the present reference
frames.explanation: Present estoy locates the ongoing activity now.

frames.label: At a past reference
frames.explanation: Imperfect estaba moves the viewpoint into a past scene. Leyendo stays unchanged.

verb-patterns.title: A small connector changes the relationship
verb-patterns.goal: Decode frequent infinitive patterns found in the stories.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: Volver a marks repetition.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.explanation: Dejar de marks stopping.

duration.title: Ongoing or completed?
duration.goal: Use desde, hace and llevar to locate a situation in time.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.spanish: Vivo aquí desde hace dos años.
frames.english: I have lived here for two years.
frames.explanation: The residence continues now.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.english: I lived there for two years.
frames.explanation: The residence is presented as a completed span.

reported-speech.title: Direct words or a later report?
reported-speech.goal: Read statements and questions reported from a past viewpoint.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: The quoted speaker uses her own present viewpoint.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.explanation: The narrator reports from a past viewpoint.

past-subjunctive.title: Assert an event or request it?
past-subjunctive.goal: Form common -ra forms and relate them to a past governing verb.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.english: He/she said he/she was explaining the system.
frames.explanation: Indicative reports an asserted explanation.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.english: He/she asked for the system to be explained.
frames.explanation: Subjunctive presents the requested action.

subjunctive-time.title: Same connector, different framing
subjunctive-time.goal: Compare factual and anticipated time clauses, including before and until.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.english: When he/she comes, he/she brings flowers.
frames.explanation: A habitual visit uses indicative viene.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.english: When he/she comes, he/she will bring flowers.
frames.explanation: A future anticipated visit uses subjunctive venga.

prepositional-pronouns.title: Owner or person after a preposition?
prepositional-pronouns.goal: Choose common prepositional pronouns and distinguish them from possessives and object pronouns.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: Mi modifies casa and has no accent.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.explanation: Mí is a standalone pronoun after para and has an accent.

narrative-connectors.title: Not yet or no longer?
narrative-connectors.goal: Use narrative markers to track sequence and expectations.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: The arrival remains expected or relevant.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.explanation: A former residence has ended.

pronominal-verbs.title: An agent causes it, or it happens to the subject
pronominal-verbs.goal: Distinguish reflexive actions, lexical pronominal verbs and common changes of state.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: Ana causes the change; la luz is the object.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.explanation: The light is the subject undergoing the change.

quantifiers.title: A noun is named or recovered
quantifiers.goal: Read common quantifiers and recognize noun omission in story references.

frames.label: Compare A
frames.explanation: The noun is expressed.

frames.label: Compare B
frames.explanation: Context supplies semilla; feminine agreement remains.
